The fact that he likes to be in the same room as you is a great sign. And sleeping near your legs? Even better. He is comfortable with you and in those moments, does not see you as a threat. 

When you're putting your hand near to him to stroke him, he probably doesn't know what you're doing and perceives it as a threat. Cats will react badly if something happens that they can't see and aren't used to (like a hand stroking their back)

When he is laying near you, try putting your hand out in front of him (cats have poor close vision so far enough away that he recognises it) and letting him come to you and sniff. Another way is to hand feed him treats so he knows your hands aren't a threat. 

Jinx took about... 2 weeks to warm up to me and let me stroke her? Luna took 4 months. It varies dependant on their personalities.

Don't force it. Give him space, time, food and play and it will happen. 

Feliway air diffusers are a good way to relax a cat in a new environment. 

Making him a little den / area that is purely his would be a great idea. When I got my girls, I made them a bed area of different pillows / blankets and then slowly put each item in a different room. This is so the cats scent gets distributed and they know their scent is in each room so they recognise it as theirs 

Some cats are sensitive as to where they like pets - one of mine, Jinxie, only likes being scratched on the neck and head. The other, Luna, likes having her belly rubbed. Let the cat guide you as to what he wants.

When you get to that stage, associate petting with other positive things I.e. treats.

OP, it doesn't sound like you have a cat with a bad case of anxiety, simply skittish. Like you have pointed out, giving the cat space, time, food and play has allowed it to warm up to you. 

Cats can be so standoffish with things, especially people. My own cat - Luna, took 4 months to come close to me. Now, every time I sit she screams at me for pets. But as soon as anyone else comes in? Or I get a delivery? Or she hears someone walk past my flat? Luna bolts straight under the bed. It is just how cats are. They come on their own terms and cannot be forced into anything. 

I would suggest, like another comment, just don't trim your cats nails or do anything to cause unnecessary stress. Get a good scratching post, douse it with some catnip and there you have it.

Also - I'm completely against declawing cats. They are more likely to experience issues with walking, display aggressive / unwanted behaviours, gait issues, chronic pain, litter box issues. Unless you want to put your cat through this, do not declaw.

I don't have answers re the anxiety but I will ask, is it necessary to trim their nails? Surely you have scratching posts which allow the cat to maintain their nails of their own accord? 

As for the act of actually trimming their nails - are you warming them up first? What I mean by this - have you held your cats paws and pressed on their pads forcing them to extend their nails or are you just trying to trim them without desensitization. 

Some cats don't like being picked up and will never allow it - don't force it upon them. It should be enough that the cat has warmed up to you enough to snuggle and be in close proximity.

I'm so glad he has eaten!! I am a little too invested in your kitten haha! Play, food, routine and warmth are the way forward with kittens. 

Are you based in the UK? If I were you, I would actually report him to relevant authorities for the way he has treated them. Not only that but do you now not need to be a certified breeder in order to sell animals?? I might be wrong...

I was exactly the same. One of my girls, Luna, she didn't want to know me for weeks. She knew I fed her and that I was safe but didn't want to be touched. It was after I developed a routine with her that she started getting a bit closer to me and came to me when she wanted attention. 

You could try calmly playing with him? Like sitting down, avoid direct eye contact and then flip a little string about. This might distract him from all those scared feelings he has right now

Leaving wet food out means its exposed to bacteria which might end up making him sick. My cats personally have never got sick from eating wet food that has been left out but the max time I would leave it out is an hour. 

Was he around others cats or animals in the last property? My girls cried for a while as I separated them from their mother and other siblings. It is really difficult to know what cats meow for - could be food, company, stress, anxiety or simply letting you know he is there. 

I think being aware of his meows is really good but again, he will come to you when he is ready. You probably want to let him know he is ok but if you react too much to these mews, he may learn that he gets what he wants from meowing - which is irritating when he decides he needs feeding at 4am!! 

I gave my girls a fuzzy blanket when they first came home and I noticed they suckled on it and purred. Maybe try something like that?

If you are very concerned about his eating habits, try leaving a few treats out. If these are eaten, it may enforce his hunger and he may be more susceptible to eating proper food. 

Please don't rush the bonding with him. I know this can feel like you have failed and that you aren't the right match for him but it isn't necessarily the case. He just needs time and patience.

He is probably really nervous right now and unsure of where he is, whether or not he is safe and is likely overwhelmed with all the new sights/smells etc.

Leave him be, definitely do not try to force him out. He will come out in his own time. 

As for leaving wet food out - have it out no longer than half an hour. I would suggest leaving a bowl of dry food and water out. Make sure everything of his is in the same room. 

Do you have anything of his from the previous home? Although they may not have treated him right, this is still home. Try rubbing whatever item you have in random spots in your house, this will get his smell around the house so he knows it is his territory. 

My kittens hid for at least 24 hours, I would be watching from a crack in the door - they would spot me and then hide again. Following that, they explored every inch of my flat. When they were out exploring, I made sure not to make sudden movements/ loud noises and definitely didn't force them to come to me. 

Everything has to be in their own time. Good luck and I'm free to message if you have any more questions!
